comparator_model: depth achieved by the landmark, alone
known_limitations_stated_in_advance: the landmark requires surviving and being assessed twice before the clock starts, so patients who progressed between the first and second scheduled assessments are excluded entirely; the cohort is therefore enriched for slower progressors and its absolute event rate is not the trial's
single-arm comparator data, so no within-patient treatment comparison is possible and the PDX selection endpoint has no human analogue in this study
roughly a sixth of nadir-clock events are regression to the mean
over half of progressions are new lesions, which have no analogue in single-implant mouse data

baseline burden and number of lesions are prognostic and are NOT in the primary model, so a C-index gain could partly reflect shape features proxying for baseline burden; the fourth sensitivity tests this directly
landmark_justification: the second scheduled tumour assessment. Chosen so that a patient on the protocol schedule has two assessments before the clock starts, which is the minimum for a rate of change. The first assessment cannot serve as a landmark because no patient has two prior scans by then.
leakage_rule: every feature must be computable from assessments STRICTLY BEFORE the landmark day; the landmark assessment itself is excluded from feature construction because it is the clock start
multiplicity: Holm across primary plus the four sensitivities
primary_event: RECIST progression from the landmark, either source
primary_metric: Harrell C-index for time to progression
question: Among patients still under observation at the landmark, does the SHAPE of the pre-landmark tumour-burden trajectory predict time to RECIST progression better than depth of response alone?
sensitivities: SLD-source events only, excluding new lesions
primary model plus log_baseline_sld as a prognostic adjustment
success_rule: trajectory C-index exceeds comparator C-index with a 95% paired bootstrap interval excluding zero
validation: 5-fold cross-validation, folds stratified on event status
